carbon_policy_signal.item: EU Commission to weaken carbon market, allowing industry more emissions; ETS reform vote stalled—carbon floor under review.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Weakened carbon discipline (EUA down 2.05% to 37th percentile) reduces fuel-switch incentive from gas to coal, flattening power-generation margins and subduing thermal dispatch merit order into autumn.

freshness_caveat: Coal data 203 days stale (as of 2025-12-26); Clean Dark 198 days stale (as of 2025-12-31). Current snapshot uses live TTF, GB Power, DE Power, renewables, storage, EUA, and Clean Spark (as of 2026-07-16–17). Coal percentile rank and daily moves not reliable for intraday trading; use spot forwarding for fuel-switch model calibration.
risk_flags: Storage at 53% (26th percentile, 15.3 pp below seasonal); refill rate will set autumn power risk if summer demand stays elevated.
EUA at 33.04 EUR/t (37th percentile) after -2.05% move; EU Commission weakening carbon market removes fuel-switch incentive, pressuring coal dispatch and power margins.
France nuclear offline mid-summer compresses baseload supply; return date unknown—GB-DE spread vulnerable if outage extends into August.
Russia oil sanctions deadline end-July at risk; price cap collapse could spike Brent, tightening LNG export economics and lifting TTF via arb.

base.summary: French nuclear remains offline; TTF consolidates 2.2σ above trend; storage refill steady. Power holds 84th percentile.

downside.summary: France nuclear restarts mid-week; EU storage refill accelerates on mild weather; Russia sanctions agreement caps Brent. TTF -4–6%; DE power -6–10%.

upside.summary: France nuclear offline extends into late July + Russia sanctions collapse; Brent spikes 8–12 USD/bbl, tightening LNG arb. TTF +5–8%; DE power +8–12%.

themes: French nuclear shutdown driving GB-DE premium, summer peaking risk
TTF extended 2.2σ above trend; storage 15.3 pp below seasonal—refill pace critical
EUA weakness (-2.05%, 2.0σ) from EU carbon market reform stall—fuel-switch disincentive
Geopolitical crude premium (Hormuz, Russia sanctions) underpinning LNG arb, indirect TTF floor
top_drivers: French nuclear shutdown mid-summer (weather-driven) compressing baseload; GB at 99th percentile as import demand surges.
EU carbon market reform stalling—EUA down 2.05% (2.0σ); weakened incentive for coal displacement, flattening power-margin arbitrage.
TTF extended 2.2σ above trend amid storage 15.3 pp below seasonal; refill pace and geopolitical crude premium (Hormuz, Russia sanctions) set summer-into-autumn gas marginal cost.
Clean Spark at 95th percentile despite coal weakness (7th percentile)—merit-order compression driven by renewable shortfall (renewables -15.29% daily, 38th percentile) and thermal call.
top_takeaway: GB Power at 99th percentile amid French nuclear offline and tight storage; Clean Spark 95th percentile; coal at 7th—fuel switch intact but carbon-policy weakness pressures margins.

watchlist.why: Carbon floor and free allocation changes determine fuel-switch economics and coal merit-order positioning this winter.
Each week offline adds ~1–2 GW import demand; DA power spread widens if heat persists into late July.
Price cap agreement or failure directly moves Brent; LNG arb sensitivity to crude means 5–10 USD/bbl swing flows 2–3 EUR/MWh into TTF.
53% fill (15.3 pp below seasonal) with TTF extended 2.2σ high—slow refill locks summer-elevated pricing into autumn marginal cost.
Persistent disruptions maintain crude risk premium, anchoring LNG export value and constraining European import opportunity cost via arbitrage.

watchlist_dated.name: Russia oil sanctions deadline (end-July negotiation window)
watchlist_dated.why: Failure to cap or extend agreement could spike Brent 5–10 USD/bbl, tightening LNG economics and lifting TTF arb floor.
